great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “the Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year… (iii) Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses…”
great.explanation: The policy reinstates your base Sum Insured unlimited times within the same year, including for the same illness. This means you have strong protection against multiple claims for the same condition without losing coverage.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: “The Recharge shall be utilized only after the base Sum Insured, 'No Claims Bonus' and 'Additional Sum Insured for Accidental Hospitalization' has been completely exhausted in that Policy Year.”
great.explanation: Extra Sum Insured is available after you exhaust your base SI and other bonuses, providing an additional layer of coverage. This helps protect you against high or multiple claims in a policy year.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 48 months of continuous coverage…”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 48 months of continuous coverage. This is a standard waiting period that balances risk and coverage.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage…”
good.explanation: The policy excludes listed illnesses and procedures for 24 months from start of coverage. This is a common waiting period for specific conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident…”
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered during the first 30 days except accidents. This is a standard initial waiting period in health insurance.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “for a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Person's date of admission to the Hospital”
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days before hospital admission are covered. This helps cover costs related to diagnosis and treatment before hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “for a period of 90 days immediately after the Insured Person's date of discharge from the Hospital”
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 90 days after discharge are covered. This supports recovery costs following hospitalization.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: “If the Policy Schedule states 'up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day' as eligible Room Rent, it means the maximum eligible Room Rent… is limited to 1% of the Sum Insured per day… If the Insured Person is admitted… higher… then… shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses…”
bad.explanation: If your policy limits room rent to 1% of Sum Insured per day, choosing a higher room category causes proportionate deductions on many hospital expenses. This can increase your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – I to Policy Terms & Conditions).”
bad.reference: Clause 4.2 Specific Exclusions (Permanent Exclusions) point 1 + Annexure I
bad.explanation: Common consumables like gloves and masks are excluded, meaning you must pay for these items yourself during hospitalization.

bad.name: NCB
bad.quote: “In the event of a Claim occurring during any Policy Year, the accrued No Claims Bonus will be reduced at same rate at which it is accrued at the commencement of next Policy Year;”
bad.explanation: Your No Claims Bonus decreases after a claim, so your Sum Insured growth is not fully protected across claims.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “The Co-payment proportion (if applicable)… (if Age… is 61 Years or above… shall bear a Co-payment of 20% per Claim…)”
bad.explanation: The policy states a 20% co-pay for ages 61 and above but does not specify co-pay for younger ages. Confirm your co-pay details in the Policy Schedule.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: “For an updated list of Network Providers… the Insured Person may refer to the list of Network Providers available on the Company's website or at the call center.”
unclear.explanation: The policy confirms cashless treatment at network hospitals but does not state how many hospitals are included. Check current network size for your area.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
